canonical_project: Nine Mile / Uinta Basin data center
aliases: Energence Utah / Nine Mile Data LLC
Nine Mile / Uinta Basin data center

location.project_area: Wells Draw Road / South Myton Bench area, southeast of Bridgeland and about six miles southwest of Myton

status_as_of_cutoff: approved-permitted: Duchesne County Planning Commission minutes record unanimous conditional-use approval on 2026-04-02; a 2026-05-26 Grand County government inventory says construction had not begun. No site-work/construction evidence was found in the 2026-08-11 refresh.
evidence_grade: A-: official Duchesne County agenda, findings report, and approved minutes verify the local CUP process/approval; construction status relies on a Utah public-notice government inventory rather than direct building-permit or site-inspection records.

actions.action_type: conditional-use public hearing and findings report
actions.result_status: Duchesne's findings report records a complete Nine Mile Data LLC application, public notice, and April 2 public hearing for a commercial data-center conditional-use permit. County minutes separately record unanimous approval at the April 2 hearing.
actions.case_or_ordinance_permit_number: Nine Mile Data LLC Data Center Development Commercial Use CUP
actions.access_caveat: Official county findings report accessible; final approval is supported by the separate April 2, 2026 Planning Commission minutes.
actions.evidence_note: Body/context retained from prior file: Duchesne County Planning Commission / Community Development.

actions.result_status: Meeting minutes list Agenda Item A6, Conditional Use Permit - Data Center, and record a motion by Commissioner Spencer Turnbow, second by Commissioner Connie Sweat, and unanimous vote to approve.
actions.access_caveat: Official county meeting minutes; the separate signed CUP instrument was not retrieved.
actions.evidence_note: The April 2 agenda describes the data-center CUP as on property owned by Vaibhav Shree LLC in the Wells Draw area.

actions.result_status: Utah Public Notice scheduled appeals by Moreen Henderson and Diana Meacham Davies of the Planning Commission's April 2 approval for the Nine Mile Data LLC data-center CUP; the same notice also covered related Wells Draw Energy and reWater appeals.
actions.access_caveat: Official notice verifies the appeals were scheduled; the official county appeal decision/minutes were not retrieved.
actions.evidence_note: Grand County's later government inventory and local reporting say resident appeals were denied, but those are not the underlying Duchesne appeal order.

actions.result_status: Utah inventory lists Nine Mile near Myton as APPROVED with Energence Utah / Nine Mile Data LLC as operator/developer and says construction had not begun; it also says resident appeals were denied. The table does not provide a MW capacity for Nine Mile; the adjacent 3,000 MW entry applies to Wonder Valley / Stratos Phase 1 in Box Elder County.
actions.access_caveat: Government compiled inventory; underlying Duchesne final CUP and appeal orders were not retrieved.
actions.evidence_note: Body/context retained from prior file: Grand County Planning Commission staff report / Utah public-notice system.

capacity_note: Official Duchesne County materials reviewed in the 2026-08-11 refresh do not state an IT/load capacity. Grand County's 2026-05-26 government inventory does not assign a MW value to Nine Mile. Cleanview lists 400 MW, but that tracker value is not treated as authoritative.

capacity_history.note: Grand County inventory table lists Nine Mile as approved with 960+ acres but no MW capacity.
Industry tracker claim; retained as non-authoritative until supported by official permit, utility, or developer material.

owner: Energence Utah, LLC / Nine Mile Data, LLC are identified in county materials as project applicant/developer entities; the April 2, 2026 county agenda/minutes list Vaibhav Shree LLC as property owner for the data-center CUP item.

sources.match_reason: Exact Phase3↔regional stable-ID pair; seed merged only with explicit evidence

contradictions.summary: A prior note interpreted 3,000 MW as Nine Mile's capacity, but the Grand County inventory table places 3,000 MW on the next row for Wonder Valley / Stratos Phase 1. Cleanview separately lists Nine Mile at 400 MW. No official Nine Mile MW capacity was found.
